Daily Workflows

Step-by-step guides for the tasks you do every day: exploring code, debugging, testing, PRs, and more.

Explore New Codebases

Just joined a project? Use Claude to ramp up fast instead of reading every file manually.

Exploration prompts

❯give me an overview of this codebase
❯explain the main architecture patterns used here
❯what are the key data models?
❯how is authentication handled?
❯find the files that handle user authentication
❯trace the login process from front-end to database
❯what coding conventions and patterns does this project use?
Start broad → go specific. Ask for a glossary of project-specific terms. Install a code intelligence plugin for your language to give Claude precise "go to definition" navigation.

Fix Bugs

Paste error messages directly. The more context you give, the faster Claude finds the root cause.

→
Paste the error
“I'm seeing this error when I run npm test: [paste error]”
→
Ask for options
“suggest a few ways to fix the @ts-ignore in user.ts”
→
Apply the fix
“update user.ts to add the null check you suggested”

Debug prompts

❯I'm seeing this error when I run npm test: [paste error here]
❯suggest a few ways to fix the null pointer in auth.ts
❯the build fails with: [paste error]. fix it and verify the build succeeds
❯trace why this function returns undefined instead of the user object

Refactor Code

bash
"color:#586e75"># In Claude:
find deprecated API usage in our codebase
"color:#586e75"># Then:
suggest how to refactor utils.js to use modern JavaScript
"color:#586e75"># Then:
refactor utils.js to ES2024 features, maintaining same behavior
"color:#586e75"># Verify:
run tests for the refactored code

Refactor prompts

❯refactor the auth module to use async/await instead of callbacks
❯find all places we use var and convert to const/let
❯split this 500-line file into smaller focused modules
❯convert these callback-based functions to use promises

Write Tests

Claude matches your existing test patterns — it reads your test files first.

Testing prompts

❯find functions in NotificationsService.swift that are not covered by tests
❯add tests for the notification service
❯add test cases for edge conditions in the notification service
❯run the new tests and fix any failures
❯write a test for foo.py covering the edge case where the user is logged out. avoid mocks
Ask Claude to "identify edge cases you might have missed" after generating the basic tests. It will suggest tests for error conditions, boundary values, and unexpected inputs.

Create Pull Requests

bash
"color:#586e75"># Simplest way:
create a pr for my changes

"color:#586e75"># Or step by step:
summarize the changes I've made to the authentication module
create a pr
enhance the PR description with more context about security improvements

When you create a PR with gh pr create, the session is automatically linked. Resume it later with:

bash
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --from-pr 123

Reference Files with @

Use @ to instantly include files without waiting for Claude to read them:

bash
"color:#586e75"># Include a single file
Explain the logic in @src/utils/auth.js

"color:#586e75"># Reference a directory listing
What's the structure of @src/components?

"color:#586e75"># Multiple files in one message
Compare @file1.js and @file2.js and suggest which pattern is better

"color:#586e75"># MCP resources
Show me the data from @github:repos/owner/repo/issues

Work with Images

Drag-and-drop images into Claude Code, or paste with Ctrl+V (not Cmd+V):

Image-related prompts

❯Analyze this image: /path/to/screenshot.png — what's causing the error?
❯Generate CSS to match this design mockup [paste image]
❯What HTML structure would recreate this component? [drag image in]
❯This is our current DB schema diagram. How should we modify it for the new feature?

Unix-Style Piping

Claude Code is composable — pipe data in, pipe structured output out:

bash
"color:#586e75"># Analyze logs in real-time
tail -f app.log | "color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "alert me if you see any anomalies"

"color:#586e75"># Review changed files for security issues
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">git diff main --name-only | "color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "review these for security issues"

"color:#586e75"># Save analysis to file
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">cat build-error.txt | "color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "explain the root cause" > analysis.txt

"color:#586e75"># Structured JSON output for scripts
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "list all API endpoints" --output-format json | jq '.[]'

"color:#586e75"># Lint-style code review in CI
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude -p "you are a linter. check for typos in changed files vs main.   report filename:line and description only"

Parallel Sessions with Git Worktrees

Work on multiple tasks simultaneously without conflicts — each session gets its own isolated copy of the codebase:

bash
"color:#586e75"># Start Claude in a new isolated worktree (new branch + directory)
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --worktree feature-auth

"color:#586e75"># Start another session on a different task simultaneously
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --worktree bugfix-payment

"color:#586e75"># Auto-generate a name
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --worktree

"color:#586e75"># Worktrees are created at ."color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude/worktrees/<name>/
"color:#586e75"># Add to .gitignore:
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">echo ".">claude/worktrees/" >> .gitignore
When you exit a worktree session with no changes, it cleans up automatically. With changes, Claude asks whether to keep or remove the branch.

Resume Previous Sessions

bash
"color:#586e75"># Continue most recent session
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --continue

"color:#586e75"># Pick from recent sessions
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --resume

"color:#586e75"># Resume by name
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --resume auth-refactor

"color:#586e75"># Resume session linked to a PR
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --from-pr 123

"color:#586e75"># Inside a session:
/rename auth-refactor    "color:#586e75"># Give current session a name
/resume                  "color:#586e75"># Open session picker
